_comment: The REAL shape of an hourly full suite killed by `timeout-minutes: 45`, taken from run
Three earlier runs that hour were identical to the second (45m17s, 45m18s, 45m17s).
The point of this fixture is the CONCLUSION: GitHub does NOT say `timed_out` when a job exceeds
its limit, it says `cancelled` — which the gate read as a gap, so the suite failing in the
loudest possible way was the one state that could never block the merge queue.
Steps are `success` up to the point of the kill, exactly as the real payload had them: a timeout
leaves no failing step to find, which is why run_death_site cannot classify it and the duration
⚠ `runner_name` IS LOAD-BEARING AND THIS FIXTURE OMITTED IT AT FIRST. The real payload carries
`canary-box` (verified against run 33986089157). Without it this fixture was indistinguishable
from a job that never got a runner, so once run_job_dispatched landed it stopped blocking — the
fix would have gone green while never firing. The positive control is what caught that: a
fixture is a COPY of reality and an omitted field is a difference, even when nothing reads it yet.
